reuse.notes: Downloadable O*NET 31.0 Database content is CC BY 4.0; credit O*NET 31.0 Database and USDOL/ETA, link the license, mark modifications, and respect O*NET trademark rules.

allowed_actions: Download database snapshots.
Store local versioned copies.
Adapt occupation/task/skill/knowledge data with attribution and modification tracking.
Crosswalk AXM professions to O*NET-SOC occupations.
forbidden_actions: Treat every O*NET field as having the same evidence method.
Import third-party content covered by a license exception without checking its separate terms.
Imply USDOL/ETA endorsement of AXM modifications.
sources.truth_scope: US occupational baseline: standardized occupation descriptors, tasks, work activities/context, skills, knowledge and related workforce descriptors. It is evidence about occupations, not a complete Professional Body or universal practice standard.
method_notes: O*NET is multi-method: fields can come from job incumbents, occupational experts, analyst ratings, employer job postings, government programs, AI/SME, machine learning, NLP, transactional data, web research and professional association input.
Preserve per-field source and date when available; software-skill evidence from employer postings is not equivalent to incumbent-rated task evidence.
sources.update_strategy: Pin exact database release and field source/date metadata; refresh against later O*NET releases by delta rather than silent replacement.

reuse.notes: Under Commission Decision 2011/833/EU, ESCO may be downloaded, used, reproduced and reused for any purpose free of charge. Acknowledge ESCO and clearly mark modified/adapted versions.

allowed_actions: Download and locally index ESCO.
Reuse occupation/skill concepts and relations with acknowledgement.
Map AXM professions to one or more ESCO concepts.
Use the downloadable Local API for offline/local-first lookup.
forbidden_actions: Treat expert-classified relevance as measured task frequency.
Hide that an AXM adaptation differs from ESCO.
Force a one-to-one AXM profession mapping when ESCO concepts are broader, narrower or adjacent.
sources.truth_scope: European labour-market classification of occupations, skills/knowledge/competences and their relationships; useful for taxonomy and crosswalk evidence rather than direct observation of one workplace.
method_notes: ESCO combines classifications, studies, job vacancies, research, stakeholder consultation and sector/occupational experts.
Occupation profiles list knowledge/skills experts considered relevant; relation semantics must remain distinct from empirical frequency or performance evidence.
sources.update_strategy: Pin ESCO version/URI and relation type; consume delta files for version changes and preserve superseded mappings.

reuse.notes: NIST employee works are generally not subject to US copyright; NIST requests attribution. Check individual artifacts for third-party/copyright markings before bulk adaptation.

allowed_actions: Use current NICE component JSON/XLSX after checking artifact markings.
Crosswalk cybersecurity professions to multiple Work Roles/Competency Areas.
Preserve Task-to-Knowledge/Skill relationships.
forbidden_actions: Treat a NICE Work Role as automatically synonymous with a job or occupation.
Assume all NIST-hosted third-party material has the same reuse status.
Treat work-role coverage as authorization or professional certification.
sources.truth_scope: Cybersecurity work decomposition into Work Roles, Competency Areas and Task/Knowledge/Skill relationships. It describes work groupings, not complete jobs or occupations.
method_notes: NICE explicitly distinguishes occupations, jobs and Work Roles; a job may contain multiple Work Roles or only part of one.
Version 2.2.0 adds/updates current component relationships and should supersede old work-role IDs when mappings changed.
sources.update_strategy: Pin component version and IDs; track NIST change logs and remap deprecated/renamed Work Roles explicitly.

reuse.notes: OOH text, charts and tables are public domain and may be reproduced with credit. Photographs are separately copyrighted and must not be ingested as public-domain content.

allowed_actions: Adapt public-domain text/charts/tables with BLS credit.
Use OOH as contextual evidence for duties, work environment, training and reported licensing context.
forbidden_actions: Ingest OOH photographs or third-party imagery as public-domain material.
Treat OOH as the authority that establishes professional licensing or practice standards.
sources.truth_scope: US occupational context and descriptive duties/work environment/entry pathways. BLS reports requirements but does not establish practicing standards.
method_notes: OOH is a standardized occupational profile resource and is useful for physical/work-environment context often absent from digital taxonomies.
sources.update_strategy: Record profile visit/update cycle and refresh contextual findings when BLS updates the occupation profile.

reuse.notes: OWASP lists ASVS under CC BY-SA 4.0. Adaptation must retain attribution and satisfy ShareAlike obligations.

allowed_actions: Reference or adapt ASVS requirements when attribution/ShareAlike obligations are satisfied.
Use machine-readable ASVS exports for requirement mapping.
forbidden_actions: Relicense adapted ASVS content incompatibly with CC BY-SA.
Treat ASVS conformance as authorization to test a target.
Treat a checklist as complete security evidence.
sources.truth_scope: Application-security verification requirements; a domain standard for control/verification coverage, not an occupation definition.
method_notes: Use alongside occupational/work-role sources rather than as a substitute for profession mapping.
sources.update_strategy: Pin ASVS version/requirement identifiers; treat later requirement renumbering or semantic changes as explicit migrations.

reuse.notes: SFIA requires a license; reproduction or distribution is prohibited unless specifically permitted. Do not bulk-ingest SFIA content into Profession Fabric without an appropriate license.

allowed_actions: Reference SFIA version/title and use licensed access within its terms.
Record that a relevant framework exists.
forbidden_actions: Copy, bulk-ingest, redistribute or derive a public rival framework from SFIA content without appropriate permission.
Treat free personal/internal access as permission for AXM public distribution.
sources.truth_scope: Licensed digital skills/responsibility framework; useful as a reference/check, not ingest material under the current AXM research policy.
method_notes: Licensing, not technical availability, controls whether content may enter the compiler.
sources.update_strategy: Reference current version metadata only until a compatible license is explicitly obtained.

reuse.notes: ISO publications are copyrighted. ISO states that, except for Open Data, ISO content may not be used for ML/AI or similar technologies without permission.

allowed_actions: Record public title, designation, edition/status and high-level public metadata.
Link to the standard as a human reference.
forbidden_actions: Ingest standard text into model/compiler context without permission.
Copy or reproduce copyrighted clauses/tables/requirements.
Infer permission from public web visibility.
sources.truth_scope: Formal standard metadata only under this policy. The standard text is not an ingest source.
method_notes: Keep independently authored professional knowledge separate from copyrighted ISO wording.
sources.update_strategy: Track edition/status metadata and supersession; never silently replace referenced editions.

reuse.notes: IEEE generally requires permission to reproduce IEEE-published text, graphics, tables or other material. Keep standards content reference-only absent explicit permission.

allowed_actions: Reference standard designation/title and public metadata.
Store links and edition status.
forbidden_actions: Reproduce standards text or tables without permission.
Bulk-ingest copyrighted standards content into public Profession Packages.
sources.truth_scope: Formal standards metadata/reference layer, not an open ingest source.
method_notes: Use open domain sources or independently authored summaries for machine-readable profession knowledge.
sources.update_strategy: Track edition and supersession metadata; request permission before changing legal mode.

reuse.notes: ISCO-08 predates ILO's newer default Creative Commons policy; exact reuse terms for a specific ISCO artifact must be checked before ingestion. Prefer ESCO's reusable ISCO mappings when possible.

allowed_actions: Reference ISCO codes/hierarchy where terms permit.
Use ESCO-provided ISCO mappings as the preferred reusable bridge.
forbidden_actions: Assume newer ILO CC terms automatically cover every pre-2023 ISCO-08 document.
Bulk-import old descriptive text without confirming its exact reuse terms.
sources.truth_scope: International occupation-classification reference; use primarily as hierarchy/crosswalk context.
method_notes: Classification units may be broader than AXM professions and are not complete professional bodies.
sources.update_strategy: Prefer reusable ESCO mappings; verify artifact-specific rights before direct ISCO content ingestion.
